title: Closed buttonhole stitch
subtitle: Pairs of bars sharing one outer point to build triangular decorative bands
excerpt: Closed buttonhole stitch groups each pair of upright bars so they meet at a shared point on the outer edge, forming a row of closed triangles. The result is a geometric decorative band rather than a plain edging, and the stitch works well on borders, ribbon-like motifs, and geometric fills.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), buttonhole stitch variations. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), closed buttonhole stitch entry.

content.text: Closed buttonhole stitch is a variation of buttonhole stitch in which each pair of bars converges to a single shared insertion point on the outer line. The first bar of a pair slants slightly to the right; the second slants to meet it at exactly the same outer hole. This creates a closed triangle for every pair, which is why the row looks geometric rather than like a plain edging.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 or 3 strands; pearl cotton no. 8 for crisper triangles

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Evenweave linen or cotton; mark a guide line before you begin

content.text: Mark two parallel guide lines with a water-soluble pen: an inner line and an outer line spaced the desired bar height apart. Fasten the thread on the back. Bring the needle up at point (A) on the inner line.

Insert the needle down at point (B) on the outer line, slightly to the right. Bring it up at point (C) on the inner line, one bar-width to the right. Pass the thread under the needle tip and pull through. This is the first bar of the pair, slanting slightly right.

For the second bar, insert the needle back into the same outer hole (B). Bring it up at point (D) on the inner line, one bar-width further right. Pass the thread under the needle tip and pull through. The two bars now share point (B) and form a closed V or triangle.

Move along the inner line to begin the next pair. Insert the needle on the outer line at a new point (E), directly below the midpoint between (C) and (D). Work the two bars of this pair so they share (E), forming the next triangle.
Continue pairing bars across the row, using a fresh shared outer point for each new triangle. Keep bar height and the angle of each slant consistent.

attrs.heading: When closed buttonhole stitch goes wrong

items.symptom: Triangles look open rather than closed
items.cause: The two bars of a pair do not share exactly the same outer hole.
items.fix: Use the tip of the needle to confirm you are entering the same hole before every second bar.

items.symptom: Row is uneven with triangles of different sizes
items.cause: The spacing between inner-line emergence points varies.
items.fix: Mark the inner-line points with a ruler or count fabric threads before starting the row.

items.cause: The thread is not sitting under the needle cleanly before pulling.
items.fix: Hold the thread down with your left thumb just below the needle tip and check the loop position before each pull.
